notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 36. My only way to reach the approved websites stopped working before I could read a single page. Every attempt came back with "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn."

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for each point and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything from memory, not even the traditional reading.

These are the pages I was going to read first. Some addresses are my best guess at the site's layout and haven't been checked:

- **Verse-by-verse:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-36/
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/36.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/36.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/36.htm
  - preceptaustin.org/psalm-36-commentary
- **Modern scholarship:** netbible.org/bible/Psalms+36 (the translators' notes, for example on "oracle" in v. 1 and "too full of conceit" in v. 2)
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** newadvent.org/fathers/1801036.htm (Augustine's exposition). I meant to check which psalm it actually covers before using it. The Latin and Greek Bibles number most psalms one lower than the Hebrew, so our Psalm 36 is usually their Psalm 35.
- **Differences between traditions:** for v. 9 ("in Your light we see light") and v. 10 ("those who know You"), searches on spurgeon.org (the Treasury of David), desiringgod.org, ligonier.org and wesley.nnu.edu.

If you ask again in a new message, the tool should be available and I'll go through this list and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point. Or, if you paste in the text of any of these pages, I can work from that straight away.
